newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan cereal and textile firm losses double.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan cereal and textile firm losses double.

text.p: Moroccan cereal and textile company Orbonor said on Tuesday it registered losses estimated at 5.7 million dirhams ($647,700) in the six months from April to September 1996.
The figure was more than double the loss for the same period in 1995 when it stood at just over two million dirhams.

A spokesman for the firm said: "We made no profit this year because of a strong competition in the textile sector and as we usually trade in November, the bad agricultural season in 1995 had a negative impact on cereals exports."
Turnover for the six months this year dropped to 230 million dirhams ($26.13 million) from 504 million dirhams in the same period in 1995.
A catastrophic drought in the 1994/95 season forced Morocco to import 2.5 million tonnes of wheat, plus other cereals, with domestic production covering only 21 percent of the demand.
